items.title: What keeps coming back to support
items.evidence_excerpt: Kendra Wallace from a retail company contacted Aegis Cloud Security support regarding severely degraded backup performance, with nightly jobs taking 4-6 hours instead of the usual 90 minutes over the past three weeks. David Kim identified a likely root cause: Kendra's environmen…
items.finding: Reliability and incidents is the primary theme on 13 of 27 support calls. Identity and access is next with 5. The raw labels underneath are fragmented (incident communication (5), feature request (4), workaround (4)). The theme is the rollup a support leader can staff against. The raw label is the evidence.

items.title: Support sentiment lags the account conversations
items.evidence_excerpt: Isaac Brennan, infrastructure lead at Trailhead Marketplace, called Aegis Cloud Security support in frustration over a complete 15+ hour outage of Aegis Detect's event processing pipeline, leaving his retail platform blind to threats. Elena Vasquez and David Kim confirmed the is…
items.finding: Support averages 2.94. External account calls average 3.71. The gap is 0.77 points on a 1–5 scale. 16 of 27 support calls score below 3.

items.title: Churn language without a recovery moment
items.evidence_excerpt: Isaac Brennan: Isaac raises PCI obligations and the risk of an undetected card skimming operation running through their checkout since the outage began
items.finding: 19 support calls contain a churn signal. 10 of them have no positive pivot in the recorded key moments. A pivot is the moment the conversation turns from the failure to a credible next step.

items.title: Feature gaps, grouped by module
items.evidence_excerpt: Gregory requests proactive seat-count threshold alerts to avoid discovering overages on future invoices
items.finding: The corpus records 51 feature-gap moments. Comply accounts for 12 of the gaps that name a module. These are not roadmap brainstorms. They are customers describing a workflow the product does not do, inside a support case or an account review.

items.title: Module sentiment is not one product story
items.evidence_excerpt: Isaac Brennan, infrastructure lead at Trailhead Marketplace, called Aegis Cloud Security support in frustration over a complete 15+ hour outage of Aegis Detect's event processing pipeline, leaving his retail platform blind to threats. Elena Vasquez and David Kim confirmed the is…
items.finding: Detect meetings average 2.73 across 22 calls that name it. Comply averages 4.28. A meeting can name more than one module. The score is the meeting score, not a sentence classifier.

items.title: The incident is a cluster, not a bad day
items.evidence_excerpt: A critical outage call was convened to address a complete failure of the Detect event processing pipeline that began around 9:14 AM Pacific. The ingestion pipeline's single primary node hit a memory ceiling and crashed due to lack of redundancy, a known tech debt issue that had…
items.finding: 10 meetings are titled as an outage, incident, or war room, from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-20. Their mean sentiment is 2.18. 53 meetings anywhere in the corpus record a technical-issue moment, so the engineering residue is larger than the bridge calendar.

items.title: Repeated failure language
items.evidence_excerpt: Megan, Raj, and Brian convened on day three of an ongoing outage affecting the Detect product's event processing pipeline. Raj explained that a single point of failure in the event ingestion layer caused a cascading failure, leaving customers with zero threat monitoring visibili…
items.finding: Across technical-issue moments and incident summaries, the strongest repeated pattern is 'Single point of failure' (15 hits). These buckets are keyword passes over the recorded technical moments, not a new root-cause model. They exist so a review can start from the language engineers and customers already used.

items.title: Accounts where the transcript is already a renewal problem
items.evidence_excerpt: Kendra Wallace: Kendra reveals Brightpath has been conducting a six-week security vendor evaluation and is seriously considering SentinelShield
items.finding: 24 accounts have at least one call with explicit churn language. The score weights repeated churn signals, a low mean, a named competitor, and a renewal already on the calendar. It is a briefing rank, not a forecast.

items.title: Which competitors the transcripts actually name
items.evidence_excerpt: Lauren Bishop: Lauren flags the March Detect outage as a major concern, noting her security team was flying blind for six hours
items.finding: SentinelShield is named in 18 meetings. The lexicon is configured, not discovered on the fly, so a new competitor does not appear until someone adds the name. The counts are meetings, not mentions, so one angry call counts once.
